Psalm

Checking which psalms are built…

Only psalms actually built on disk can be encoded — the rest are shown as “not built yet”. What counts as built is read from tools/built-psalms.json (a psalm counts as built when both its data file and its cartridge exist on disk; re-run tools/build_built_psalms.py after building a psalm — if the manifest is missing the page falls back to probing for each data file instead). On file:// only Psalm 1 is offered: its chapter data and audio are embedded in this page as fallbacks (embedding all 150 psalms would bloat the page — each carries its own audio — so the other psalms need this page served over HTTP). A psalm picked here can also be linked directly, e.g. psalms/encode.html?psalm=23.

Numbers — check before you encode

Full quality by default: the cartridge holds the complete, unmodified models, audio and text. The only compression is lossless zlib (decoded bytes identical) — nothing lossy is ever applied.

Only for this image being too small to hold the models: the cartridge records the models as remote links instead of packing them in. Its world will then need the network, and the decoder will always warn that the cartridge is not fully offline. Off by default — turn it on only if you mean it. A bigger cover image is the fully-offline option.
